description: FILED s446j (agent J), while fixing #506; PRE-EXISTING.  Repro: `no strict; no warnings; $?{"k"} = "V"; my @k = keys %?;` -- perl 1 key, PCL drops the statement ("Handle single node of unknown type").  Measured over all 29 punctuation characters: the ELEMENT spellings ($X{k} / $X[0]) all work since #506 owns the containers, and the whole-container spellings all drop.  Mechanism (PPI 1.291, dumped): `keys %?` is Word(keys) + Operator(%) + Operator(?), never a Symbol -- the same mis-lex as docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md sec.24 for `@?`, which Pl::Parser::_merge_punct_array_symbols repairs on ADJACENCY.  Why the hash twin is not the same one-line widening: a `@` Cast can only ever be a sigil, while `%` is also the MODULO operator (`$a % $b`), so the repair needs a position rule -- fire only where a TERM is expected (after keys/values/each, `=`, `(`, `,`, a list operator).  `%$;` is worse still: PPI swallows the `;` into a Magic($;).  Bar: the repro for %? and %$, the modulo INVERSE (`$a % $b`, `$a %$b`, `5 % 3`) unchanged, a row beside Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t.  NOTE: #449 is the ARRAY half of the same family and its stated blocker is now gone -- the emitter pipe-quotes the CL-unsafe names already (|@,| |@;| |@\||, verified) and s446j made the runtime own every one of them, so widening %PUNCT_ARRAY_CHARS to the full set is unblocked and belongs with this task.
subject: The WHOLE-CONTAINER spelling of a punctuation hash or array still DROPS (`keys %$`, `%? = (...)`): PPI lexes `%?` as Operator+Operator and the repair covers only the `@` half, because `%` is ambiguous with modulo
